name: בֵּית רָפָא
gloss: house of Rapha; or house of healing
summary: A son of Eshton in the genealogy of Judah, named once, with his brothers Paseah and Tehinnah “the father of Ir-nahash”; “these are the men of Recah” (1Ch 4:12). The name is בֵּית, “house of”, with רָפָא. It is the only name of this shape that scripture gives to a man as begotten, and it is shaped like the names of towns and clans: the same lists call Salma “the father of Bethlehem”, Hareph “the father of Beth-gader” and Maon “the father of Beth-zur” (1Ch 2:45, 51), where a man is the father of a settlement, and Tehinnah in this very verse is the father of a town. So “Beth-rapha” may be the household or clan of a man Rapha, begotten by Eshton in the sense that it sprang from him. רָפָא is itself a man’s name (1Ch 8:2) and the name of the forefather of the giants of Gath, הָרָפָא (1Ch 20:6, 8); as a verb it is “heal” (Exo 15:26). Scripture does not explain the name, so which is meant is not shown.

evidence.note: “Eshton begot בֵּית רָפָא and Paseah and Tehinnah the father of Ir-nahash. These are the men of Recah.”
Eshton son of Mehir, son of Chelub.
“Salma the father of Bethlehem, Hareph the father of Beth-gader”: Beth- names as what a man fathers.
רָפָא, the fifth son of Benjamin: a man’s name.
The man of great stature at Gath “was born to הָרָפָא”; so verse 8.
The verb: “I am Yahweh who heals you (רֹפְאֶךָ).”
בֵּית אָב, a man’s house as the family that comes from him.

note: TIPNR records Beth-rapha as a person (son of Eshton), and the key b.bp.bu is his alone; its one counted token is the word רָפָא, the בֵּית before it being counted with the noun. Whether a man or a clan is meant is left open, as the verse leaves it. The second half belongs to רפא, which has no entry yet; when it has, the reading “house of the healer” or “of Rapha” should be checked against it.
